# Rethinking Epicenter's file editor: one buffer, with independent facts about storage ## Current state in this snapshot The nested proposal is already implemented here. `BufferSnapshot` has the shape `unread | loading | unavailable | ready{text, unsaved?}` (`packages/folder/src/edit-owner.ts:141`), and the README documents it (`packages/folder/README.md:244`). I couldn't read the threads or the live branch, so this describes only the snapshot. Five behaviours in the code bear on your questions: - **Callers merge `dirty` and `saving`.** Epicenter (`FileEditor.svelte:81`) and Capture (`TextDetail.svelte:157-162`) show both as "Saving…". Whispering calls "held and not failed" `isSaving` (`whispering.svelte.ts:1039-1041`). - **Typing clears an older failure.** New text clears a non-conflict error (`edit-owner.ts:1153`, `:860`). A retry also clears the error as soon as it starts (`:847`). - **`save()` can report on the wrong text.** If newer text was typed but not yet tried, the save loop can end and return the older revision's failure (`:871`, `:888`). - **A clean file deleted elsewhere loses its text.** The buffer becomes `unavailable` with no text. Epicenter works around this by keeping its own `lastShown` copy (`FileEditor.svelte:54-64`). - **Typing doesn't clear a conflict** (`:1153`). ## Central answer: no single five-way status **Your hypothesis holds.** `clean | dirty | saving | failed | conflict` blends three independent facts and then picks one to display: 1. **Is the text unsaved?** This compares the current text with storage. 2. **Is a write running?** That write may contain older text. 3. **What stopped the last write?** Either a failure or a conflict. Real sequences combine these facts. You can type during a save (unsaved and saving). You can retry a failure (saving, and the failure still applies). You can type after a conflict (unsaved, and the conflict still applies). A single union has to hide one fact in each of these cases. A union is still right for the third fact. A failure and a conflict carry different payloads and offer different actions, and they can't both be true at once, so they belong in one union. ## Organizing idea **The editor *is* the file-backed buffer, and it always has text.** Loading belongs to *acquiring* an editor, not to the editor. Once you have one, it holds text, a revision number, and a fixed set of facts about how that text relates to storage. The folder still owns one buffer per path. Handles share it, and it outlives the components that show it. ```ts // Acquisition: async, outside the editing component const opened = await folder.open('notes/a.md', { schema: noteSchema }); // Result, ReadError | Missing | NotText> // Resolves immediately if the folder already holds this path's buffer. // folder.held(path): Editor | undefined, synchronous, for remounts and recovery. type Editor = { readonly path: string; readonly text: string; // always present readonly markdown: MarkdownContent; // the same text, read through the schema readonly revision: number; // +1 for each accepted change readonly dirty: boolean; // revision > savedRevision readonly saving: boolean; // a write is running (maybe of an older revision) readonly problem?: // why the last write didn't land | { name: 'Failed'; at: number; error: SaveFailure } | { name: 'Conflict'; base: string | null; current: FileContent | null }; readonly readError?: ReadError; // the last refresh failed; text unaffected readonly locked?: string; // a fenced action holds the path readonly ended?: 'deleted' | 'not-text' | 'closed'; // the editor is finished; text stays copyable replaceText(text: string): ChangeResult; change(change: DocumentChange): ChangeResult; save(): Promise>; revert(): void; // new revision whose text is the saved text keepMine(text?: string): Promise; // resolve a conflict: overwrite storage takeTheirs(): void; // resolve a conflict: take storage's text, no write discard(): Recovery | undefined; subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void; release(): void; // drop this handle; held text survives }; ``` ## Definitions - **Base (the witness):** the exact source storage was last known to hold, `null` for "no file". Every write is checked against the base inside the guarded storage call. - **Saved revision:** the newest revision whose text storage has confirmed. **Saved** means `revision === savedRevision`. - **Dirty:** `revision > savedRevision`. Changing the text back doesn't rewind it: - With no write running, a change whose text equals the base is marked saved immediately. - While a write runs, that same change stays dirty, because storage is about to change. - **`save()`:** captures `r = revision` and resolves when revision `r` or a newer one lands, returning that revision. It resolves with an error only if a write *containing r or newer* fails. It never reports an older revision's outcome. - **Flush:** cancel the autosave pause and save now. `editor.save()` flushes one path. `folder.flush()`, today's `settle`, flushes every dirty path and returns what remains unsaved. - **Saved ≠ durable:** saved means storage acknowledged the write. Crash recovery of in-memory text is a separate journal, and none of these terms promise it. - **Error lifetimes:** - A **conflict** describes the base, so it lasts until `keepMine` or `takeTheirs`. Typing doesn't clear it, and autosave stops because it would only conflict again. - A **failure** describes an attempt. It stays until a later write lands or the text becomes clean again. A retry keeps the old failure visible while it runs, then either clears it or replaces it. Typing after a failure triggers a normal autosave of the new revision, but the same revision is never retried automatically. - A **read error** concerns observing storage, not saving. The next successful read clears it. ## Five sequences **1. Typing during a save.** Revision r5 is being written and you type r6, so the editor is `saving` and `dirty`. When r5 lands, `savedRevision` becomes 5 and the base becomes r5's text. The editor is still dirty, and autosave writes r6. A `save()` called during r5 resolves after r5 lands. One called after r6 waits for r6. **2. Reverting while a save runs.** The base is T4 and r5 (text T5) is being written. `revert()` creates r6 with text T4, which stays dirty. - If r5 lands, the base becomes T5, and r6 is written to restore T4. - If r5 fails, storage still holds T4, which equals r6. The editor becomes clean with no write, and the failure disappears because no unsaved text remains. **3. Retrying a failure.** r5 failed, so `problem` is `Failed{at: 5}`. Calling `save()` starts a write while `problem` stays set, so the UI can show "Retrying…". Success clears `problem`. Another failure replaces it with the new error. **4. Typing after a conflict.** Saving r5 hit a conflict: storage holds C. You type r6. The conflict remains and autosave stays stopped. Three ways out: - `keepMine()` makes C the base and writes r6. - `takeTheirs()` sets the text to C as a new revision, already saved. - To merge, call `replaceText(mergeText(base, C, text))`, then `keepMine()`. **5. Refreshing while text is usable.** - **The read fails:** `readError` is set, and the text and editing are untouched. - **The file was deleted and the editor is clean:** the editor follows storage, so `ended: 'deleted'`. The text stays readable and copyable. Epicenter's `lastShown` workaround goes away. - **The file was deleted and the editor is dirty:** the editor reports `Conflict{current: null}` immediately. The next save would have discovered the same fact. `keepMine()` recreates the file; `takeTheirs()` ends the editor. Your question about always-retained text gets an explicit answer in the clean-deletion case. The editor keeps the text but stops accepting changes, so a file deleted elsewhere is never silently brought back. ## Vanilla use ```ts const opened = await folder.open(path); if (opened.error) return showOpenError(opened.error); const editor = opened.data; editor.replaceText(next); // accepted into memory, autosaves after the pause const saved = await editor.save(); // covers every revision up to this call if (saved.error?.name === 'Conflict') showCompare(editor.problem); editor.release(); // dirty text stays held by the folder ``` ## Svelte ```svelte {#await folder.open(path)} {:then opened} {#if opened.error} {:else}{#key path}{/key}{/if} {/await} ``` ```svelte {#if conflict}Saved file changed {:else if editor.saving}{editor.problem ? 'Retrying…' : 'Saving…'} {:else if editor.problem}Not saved: {editor.problem.error.message} {:else if editor.dirty}Edited {:else}Saved{/if} {#if conflict} {:else if editor.problem && !editor.saving} {/if} {#if editor.ended === 'deleted'}

Deleted elsewhere. Copy anything you need.

{/if} {#if editor.readError}

Couldn't check for outside changes. Your text is kept.

{/if}
